title: CLAUDE.md
code: wjp_newchart <- function(data, target, grouping, colors = NULL, cvec = NULL,                          ptheme = WJP_theme(), show_legend = FALSE) {   # 1. Rename columns with all_of()   data <- data %>% rename(target_var = all_of(target), grouping_var = all_of(grouping))    # 2. Handle NULL/duplicate parameters   if (is.null(colors) || identical(colors, grouping)) {     data <- data %>% mutate(colors_var = grouping_var)   } else {     data <- data %>% rename(colors_var = all_of(colors))   }    # 3. Fall back to the WJP palette when no color vector is supplied   if (is.null(cvec)) cvec <- wjp_default_cvec(data$colors_var)    # 4. Create ggplot (text layers use family = wjp_font_family())   plt <- ggplot(data, aes(...)) + geom_*(show.legend = show_legend) +     scale_fill_manual(values = cvec, breaks = wjp_legend_breaks(data$colors_var), name = NULL)    # 5. Apply theme, chart-specific tweaks, and the shared legend; then the   #    user's ptheme overrides, always last   plt <- plt + ptheme + theme(...) + wjp_legend_theme(show_legend)   plt <- wjp_apply_ptheme(plt, ptheme)    return(plt) }

title: Contributing to WJPr
text: Every chart function follow structure:
code: #' Short descriptive title #' #' @description #' `r lifecycle::badge("experimental")` #' #' Detailed description of what the function does. #' #' @param data Data frame containing the data to plot. #' @param target String. Column name of the variable that supplies the values. #' @param ... other parameters #' #' @return A ggplot object. #' @export #' #' @examples #' # Complete, reproducible example #' wjp_newfunction <- function(     data,     target,     grouping,     colors      = NULL,     cvec        = NULL,     labels      = NULL,     ptheme      = WJP_theme(),     show_legend = FALSE ) {    # ===========================================================================   # 1. RENAME VARIABLES   # ===========================================================================   # Use all_of() to rename columns safely   data <- data %>%     rename(       target_var   = all_of(target),       grouping_var = all_of(grouping)     )    # Handle optional parameters with NULL checks   if (is.null(colors) || identical(colors, grouping)) {     data <- data %>%       mutate(colors_var = grouping_var)   } else {     data <- data %>%       rename(colors_var = all_of(colors))   }    # ===========================================================================   # 2. TRANSFORM DATA (if needed)   # ===========================================================================   # Calculations, ordering, etc.    # ===========================================================================   # 3. DEFAULT COLORS   # ===========================================================================   # Fall back to the WJP palette when no color vector is supplied   if (is.null(cvec)) {     cvec <- wjp_default_cvec(data$colors_var)   }    # ===========================================================================   # 4. CREATE THE BASE CHART   # ===========================================================================   plt <- ggplot(data, aes(x = grouping_var, y = target_var, fill = colors_var)) +     geom_col(show.legend = show_legend) +     geom_text(       aes(label = target_var),       family   = wjp_font_family(),       fontface = "bold",       size     = 3.514598,       color    = "#4a4a49"     ) +     scale_fill_manual(       values = cvec,       breaks = wjp_legend_breaks(data$colors_var),       name   = NULL     )    # ===========================================================================   # 5. APPLY THEME AND FINAL TWEAKS   # ===========================================================================   plt <- plt +     ptheme +     theme(       # Chart-specific tweaks     ) +     wjp_legend_theme(show_legend)    # Always last: user overrides passed through `ptheme`   plt <- wjp_apply_ptheme(plt, ptheme)    return(plt) }

text: wjp_bars() function can also used create stacked bar charts. instance, instead plotting percentage respondents “lot” “” trust Institution , can visualize percentage distribution possible responses country. First, modify data reflect new design: Notice transform q1a column factor variable define specific levels (order) responses. Specifying factor levels allows us control answers displayed chart. don’t define factor levels, responses default alphabetical order, may align intended order ordinal variable. data ready, can use wjp_bars() function , time setting stacked parameter TRUE (value labels drawn white inside segment) show_legend = TRUE (readers can identify answer):
code: data4stackedbars <- gpp_data %>%   filter(     year == 2022   ) %>%   select(country, q1a) %>%   mutate(     q1a = as.double(unclass(q1a)),     q1a  = case_when(       q1a == 1  ~ "A lot",       q1a == 2  ~ "Some",       q1a == 3  ~ "Little",       q1a == 4  ~ "None",       q1a == 99 ~ "No answer",     ),     q1a = factor(       q1a,        levels = c("A lot", "Some", "Little", "None", "No answer")     )   ) %>%   group_by(country, q1a) %>%   count() %>%   group_by(country) %>%   arrange(country, desc(q1a)) %>%   mutate(     total       = sum(n),     percentage  = (n/total)*100,     value_label = paste0(       format(         round(percentage, 1),         nsmall = 1       ),       "%"     ),     value_label = if_else(percentage >= 5, value_label, NA_character_),     label_position = cumsum(percentage)-(percentage/2)   ) %>%   select(     country, q1a, percentage, value_label, label_position   )  kbl(data4stackedbars) stacked_bar <- wjp_bars(     data4stackedbars,     target      = "percentage",     grouping    = "country",     labels      = "value_label",     lab_pos     = "label_position",     colors      = "q1a",     cvec        = c("A lot"     = "#482d8b",                     "Some"      = "#2894aa",                     "Little"    = "#869d3b",                     "None"      = "#f26b21",                     "No answer" = "#555659"),     direction   = "horizontal",     stacked     = TRUE,     show_legend = TRUE )  stacked_bar

code: #' Plot a Waterfall Chart following WJP style guidelines #' #' @description #' `r lifecycle::badge("experimental")` #' #' `wjp_waterfall()` creates a waterfall chart showing the cumulative effect #' of sequential positive and negative values. #' #' @param data Data frame containing the data to plot. #' @param target String. Column name with numeric values to plot. #' @param grouping String. Column name with category labels. #' @param colors String. Column name for color grouping. Default is `NULL`. #' @param cvec Named vector of colors. Default is `NULL` (the WJP palette, #'   see [wjp_palette()], is applied). #' @param labels String. Column name with value labels. Default is `NULL`. #' @param direction String. `"horizontal"` or `"vertical"`. Default is `"vertical"`. #' @param ptheme ggplot theme to apply. Default is [WJP_theme()]. #' @param show_legend Logical. If `TRUE`, displays a horizontal legend above #'   the chart. Default is `FALSE`. #' #' @return A ggplot object representing the waterfall chart. #' @export #' #' @examples #' # Always load the WJP fonts #' wjp_fonts() #' #' # Prepare data #' data_waterfall <- data.frame( #'   category = c("Start", "Gain A", "Loss B", "Gain C", "End"), #'   value    = c(100, 30, -20, 15, 125), #'   type     = c("total", "positive", "negative", "positive", "total") #' ) #' #' # Create chart #' wjp_waterfall( #'   data_waterfall, #'   target   = "value", #'   grouping = "category", #'   colors   = "type", #'   cvec     = c("total"    = "#482d8b", #'                "positive" = "#0f9581", #'                "negative" = "#f26b21") #' )  wjp_waterfall <- function(     data,     target,     grouping,     colors      = NULL,     cvec        = NULL,     labels      = NULL,     direction   = "vertical",     ptheme      = WJP_theme(),     show_legend = FALSE ) {    # ===========================================================================   # SECTION 1: INPUT VALIDATION (optional but recommended)   # ===========================================================================    if (!is.data.frame(data)) {     stop("`data` must be a data frame.", call. = FALSE)   }    if (!target %in% names(data)) {     stop("Column '", target, "' not found in `data`.", call. = FALSE)   }    if (!direction %in% c("vertical", "horizontal")) {     stop('`direction` must be one of "vertical" or "horizontal".', call. = FALSE)   }    # ===========================================================================   # SECTION 2: RENAME VARIABLES   # ===========================================================================    # Rename the required columns   data <- data %>%     dplyr::rename(       target_var   = dplyr::all_of(target),       grouping_var = dplyr::all_of(grouping)     )    # Handle the colors column   if (is.null(colors) || identical(colors, grouping)) {     # If not supplied (or the same column as grouping), reuse grouping     data <- data %>%       dplyr::mutate(colors_var = grouping_var)   } else {     data <- data %>%       dplyr::rename(colors_var = dplyr::all_of(colors))   }    # Handle labels   if (is.null(labels)) {     data <- data %>%       dplyr::mutate(labels_var = "")   } else if (identical(labels, grouping)) {     data <- data %>%       dplyr::mutate(labels_var = grouping_var)   } else if (identical(labels, colors)) {     data <- data %>%       dplyr::mutate(labels_var = colors_var)   } else {     data <- data %>%       dplyr::rename(labels_var = dplyr::all_of(labels))   }    # ===========================================================================   # SECTION 3: DATA TRANSFORMATIONS   # ===========================================================================    # Compute the waterfall positions   data <- data %>%     dplyr::mutate(       end   = cumsum(target_var),       start = dplyr::lag(end, default = 0),       # Handle negative values       ymin  = pmin(start, end),       ymax  = pmax(start, end)     )    # ===========================================================================   # SECTION 4: DEFAULT COLORS   # ===========================================================================    # Fall back to the WJP palette when no color vector is supplied   if (is.null(cvec)) {     cvec <- wjp_default_cvec(data$colors_var)   }    # ===========================================================================   # SECTION 5: BASE CHART   # ===========================================================================    plt <- ggplot2::ggplot(     data,     ggplot2::aes(       x    = grouping_var,       fill = colors_var     )   ) +     ggplot2::geom_rect(       ggplot2::aes(         xmin = as.numeric(factor(grouping_var)) - 0.4,         xmax = as.numeric(factor(grouping_var)) + 0.4,         ymin = ymin,         ymax = ymax       ),       show.legend = show_legend     ) +     ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(       values = cvec,       breaks = wjp_legend_breaks(data$colors_var),       name   = NULL     )    # Add value labels if supplied   if (!all(data$labels_var == "")) {     plt <- plt +       ggplot2::geom_text(         ggplot2::aes(           x     = grouping_var,           y     = ymax,           label = labels_var         ),         vjust    = -0.5,         family   = wjp_font_family(),         fontface = "bold",         size     = 3.514598,         color    = "#4a4a49"       )   }    # ===========================================================================   # SECTION 6: DIRECTION   # ===========================================================================    if (direction == "horizontal") {     plt <- plt +       ggplot2::coord_flip()   }    # ===========================================================================   # SECTION 7: THEME AND FINAL TWEAKS   # ===========================================================================    plt <- plt +     ptheme +     ggplot2::labs(x = "", y = "") +     ggplot2::theme(       panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank()     ) +     wjp_legend_theme(show_legend)    # Always last: user overrides passed through `ptheme`   plt <- wjp_apply_ptheme(plt, ptheme)    return(plt) }

code: data_slope <- gpp_data %>%   filter(year %in% c(2017, 2019)) %>%   mutate(     q1a   = as.double(unclass(q1a)),     gend  = as.double(unclass(gend)),     trust  = case_when(q1a <= 2 ~ 1, q1a <= 4 ~ 0),     gender = case_when(gend == 1 ~ "Male", gend == 2 ~ "Female")   ) %>%   group_by(year, gender) %>%   summarise(trust = mean(trust, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, .groups = "drop") %>%   mutate(label = paste0(round(trust, 0), "%"))  wjp_slope(   data_slope,   target   = "trust",   grouping = "year",   colors   = "gender",   labels   = "label",   cvec     = c("Male" = "#482d8b", "Female" = "#f26b21"),   repel    = TRUE,   show_legend = TRUE )

text: wjp_radar() - Compare multiple dimensions circular grid.  Expected input structure — long format: one row per axis_var (dimension) × colors (group). labels gives human-readable axis name, show_legend = TRUE identifies compared groups. Input data wjp_radar(): target = score, axis_var = category, colors = gender
code: data_radar <- gpp_data %>%   select(gend, starts_with("q49")) %>%   mutate(     gend = as.double(unclass(gend)),     across(starts_with("q49"), \(x) as.double(unclass(x))),     gender = case_when(gend == 1 ~ "Male", gend == 2 ~ "Female"),     across(starts_with("q49"), ~ case_when(.x <= 2 ~ 1, .x <= 99 ~ 0))   ) %>%   group_by(gender) %>%   summarise(across(starts_with("q49"), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE) * 100), .groups = "drop") %>%   pivot_longer(-gender, names_to = "category", values_to = "score") %>%   mutate(     label = case_when(       category == "q49a"    ~ "Reliable",       category == "q49b_G1" ~ "Accessible",       category == "q49b_G2" ~ "Channels",       category == "q49c_G1" ~ "Consistent",       category == "q49c_G2" ~ "Stable",       category == "q49d_G1" ~ "Efficient",       category == "q49d_G2" ~ "Fast",       category == "q49e_G1" ~ "Effective",       category == "q49e_G2" ~ "Trustworthy"     )   )  wjp_radar(   data_radar,   axis_var = "category",   target   = "score",   labels   = "label",   colors   = "gender",   cvec     = c("Male" = "#482d8b", "Female" = "#f26b21"),   show_legend = TRUE )

title: Chart Gallery
text: wjp_groupbars() - Faceted bars compare value across demographic groups (one facet per grouping). Values can supplied proportions (0-1) percentages (0-100). Confidence intervals can calculated sd sample_size, supplied directly ci_lower ci_upper. national/general value can added either bar (national_style = "bar") vertical reference line (national_style = "line").  Expected input structure — one row per levels category, tagged grouping (facet) belongs target value. target, national_value, ci_lower, ci_upper may proportions percentages. draw confidence interval bar, set draw_ci = TRUE either supply per-category sd plus sample_size, pass precomputed ci_lower ci_upper columns. national_style = "bar", national value inserted regular bar row can receive national_ci_lower national_ci_upper. second color represents complement 100%, neutral gray keeps attention measured percentage interval. Input data wjp_groupbars(): target = value, grouping = group, levels = category, lower/upper confidence intervals
code: # Percentage-scale input with precomputed confidence intervals. data_groupbars <- data.frame(   group    = c("Gender", "Gender", "Age", "Age", "Age"),   category = c("Men", "Women", "18-24", "25-54", "55+"),   value    = c(74.4, 70.3, 72.1, 73.1, 73.0),   lower    = c(72.4, 68.4, 70.1, 71.0, 70.8),   upper    = c(76.4, 72.1, 74.5, 75.2, 75.2) )  wjp_groupbars(   data_groupbars,   target            = "value",   grouping          = "group",   levels            = "category",   colors            = c("#482d8b", "#e5e8e8"),   group_order       = c("Gender", "Age"),   level_order       = list(     Gender = c("Men", "Women"),     Age    = c("18-24", "25-54", "55+")   ),   draw_ci           = TRUE,   ci_lower          = "lower",   ci_upper          = "upper",   show_national     = TRUE,   national_value    = 72.3,   national_style    = "bar",   national_label    = "National Average",   national_ci_lower = 70.0,   national_ci_upper = 74.6,   show_axis         = TRUE )

title: WJP ggplot2 Theme — WJP_theme
text: family String. Font family text elements. Default active WJP font family (see wjp_font_family()), "Lato Full" unless changed via options(wjpr.family = ). base_size Numeric. Size axis text titles, points. Default 10. text_colour String. Color axis text titles. Default "#524F4C". WJP country reports use "#1A1A1A". grid String. Major grid lines draw: "major" (directions, default), "x" (lines breaks x scale), "y" (lines breaks y scale), "none". grid_colour String. Color grid lines. Default "#5e5c5a". grid_linetype Line type grid lines. Default "dashed". base_theme complete ggplot2 theme start (e.g., ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11)). Default NULL (partial theme).

title: WJP ggplot2 Theme — WJP_theme
text: theme includes following style specifications: Transparent panel plot backgrounds Dashed grey grid lines (#5e5c5a) WJP font family text elements (Lato Full default; see wjp_font_family()). family also set root text element, titles, legends, strips inherit . Axis text titles base_size points #524F4C axis ticks Zero plot margins WJP_theme() partial theme: added top active complete theme (ggplot2's ggplot2::theme_grey() unless set another one). Use base_theme start different complete theme, ggplot2::theme_minimal(). passed ptheme argument WJPr chart function, elements differ default WJP_theme() applied chart's styling, take precedence (example, WJP_theme(base_size = 9) resizes axis labels every chart). percentage / 2     )   ) %>%   ungroup()  wjp_bars(   data4stacked,   target   = "percentage",   grouping = "country",   labels   = "value_label",   lab_pos  = "label_position",   colors   = "level",   stacked  = TRUE,   show_legend = TRUE,   cvec     = c("Trust" = "#482d8b", "No trust" = "#f26b21") )   # Country and EU average side by side, with a 100% track and values after # each bar (fictional data) paired <- data.frame(   category = rep(c("Consumer", "Housing", "Employment"), 2),   series   = rep(c("Atlantis", "EU Average"), each = 3),   value    = c(40, 10, 19, 21, 7, 10) ) paired$text <- paste0(paired$value, "%")  wjp_bars(   paired,   target         = "value",   grouping       = "category",   labels         = "text",   colors         = "series",   cvec           = c("Atlantis" = "#575796", "EU Average" = "#A8A8C8"),   direction      = "horizontal",   position       = "dodge",   track          = TRUE,   value_position = "outside",   value_colors   = c("Atlantis" = "#575796", "EU Average" = "#7D7DA8"),   value_axis     = FALSE,   grid           = FALSE,   label_align    = "right",   show_legend    = TRUE,   layout         = wjp_layout(label_width = 90, label_gap = 6,                               track_width = 250, value_gap = 5,                               value_width = 30, row_height = 21,                               bar_height = 8) )
